entries.question: Why is the Chinese V41 package 34.8 MB while the international one is 5.8 MB?
evidence: results/firmware/v41-chinese-vs-international.md
research/firmware/2026-09-28/v41-chinese-vs-international.json
entries.answer: The Chinese ZIP bundles the 28,032,675-byte Android app BIGBIG_WON_2.22.1226.apk plus Chinese-only change-log text files; the international RAR does not. All firmware payloads and all seven BTUpgrade_V1.9 files are byte-identical.

entries.question: Are the actual V41 firmware payload bytes identical between the CN and international packages?
evidence: same SHA-256 for 01战甲X Pro固件-V41.bup and Firmware ArmorX-Pro V41.bup; same for both V3600 dongle .bup files; all 7 updater files identical
entries.answer: YES

entries.question: What exactly is inside V2224.bup / the V32 / V41 / dongle packages?
evidence: results/firmware/bup-format.md
tools/firmware/armorx_bup.py
entries.answer: BUP = 'BigBigWon Upgrade Pack' header + one or two sub-images, each stored as a sequence of independent zlib blocks of 32,768 B preceded by (compressed,uncompressed) u32 records. Decompressed result is a raw JieLi JLFS flash image.
ruled_out: custom encryption on the BUP container itself (plain zlib)

entries.question: Can the official updater decrypt/decompress the BUP?
evidence: BUP payload is plain zlib — no updater is needed to decompress it; encryption lives in the flash image (ENC/chip-key), which the JieLi unpacker already decrypted offline
entries.answer: Not needed for decompression. The updater's remaining role (device detection, transfer protocol, verification) has not yet been read statically.
entries.next_offline_step: PE static analysis of BUpgrade.exe / Upgrade.dll / BTUpgrade.dll / Devices.dll in the extracted BTUpgrade_V1.9 tree

entries.question: Is the ArmorX firmware JieLi .ufw / jl_isd.fw / JLFS or another JieLi format?
evidence: format: jl-new-fw from jl-misctools fwunpack_newfw.py
chip AC632N, PID AC632N_TRANS, uboot.boot + isd_config.ini + app_dir_head + VM + key_mac + BTIF/EXIF/USERIF
JLBTSDKflash, 632N_LE_UPDATE, ble_ota.bin/edr_ota2.bin
entries.answer: JieLi JLFS flash image in the 'jl-new-fw' layout (not the older .ufw container despite the .ufw slot names) running on an AC632N/AC6321A.

entries.question: Which image runs on AC6321A?
evidence: board_ac6321a.c source path inside decrypted app.bin
app base 0x01E00000, entry 0x01E00120
chip name AC632N / PID AC632N_TRANS
entries.answer: The body app.bin (227,440 B for V41) runs on the AC6321A.

entries.question: Does that image contain our known A5/A4/AB protocol?
evidence: A real frame dispatcher exists: 'out cmd=%x,%x pa=%x, len=%d', 'in cmd=%x,%x', 'unsupport cmd: 0x%x', 'cmd head err', 'cmd len err', 'cmd sum err'
literal A5/A4/AB byte sequences are absent from app.bin (expected for compiled code)
entries.answer: Partly: string xrefs now resolve into the image and the A5 frame handler exists, but no plaintext A5/A4/AB constant table was found. The dispatcher compares the opcode against D2/D4/D7/F7/F8/F9/FA/FF, which matches the live families.
ruled_out: the protocol is implemented in a separate, absent image (the app contains the dispatcher)
entries.next_offline_step: Disassemble app.bin with a BD19/q32s disassembler and resolve the dispatcher's opcode table; or match against the AC63 SDK HID/gamepad app

entries.question: Is firmware authenticity verified cryptographically or merely checksum-protected?
evidence: BUP container: no signature field observed (magic + version + names + sizes + zlib)
flash image: uboot.boot is 'compressed: true'; CRC/hash machinery (CRC16/CRC32) is present in the JieLi toolchain and the image uses checksums
no RSA/ECDSA signature blob located
isd_config.ini carries a chip key, which is CONFIDENTIALITY (ENC obfuscation), not AUTHENTICITY
entries.answer: Evidence so far points to checksum/CRC integrity plus a confidentiality-only chip key; no cryptographic signature found. NOT sufficient to claim 'no secure boot'.
ruled_out: signature visible in the BUP container
entries.next_offline_step: Read the updater's verification branch and locate the firmware CRC/hash check in app.bin

entries.question: Is there one MCU doing most of the ArmorX logic, or is AC6321A only a communications coprocessor?
evidence: decrypted app.bin contains config engine, macro engine, stick/trigger curves, gyro handling, USB host+device, 2.4G select, console DEV_TYPE conversion, flash write
vendor identity ZIKWAY/ZJ-XT* inside the image
entries.answer: STRONG EVIDENCE the AC6321A is the main application MCU, not a thin bridge. A possible secondary MCU (RF front-end / sensor hub) is neither proven nor excluded.
ruled_out: AC6321A is a pure BLE/OTA bridge
entries.next_offline_step: Check whether the app talks to a second MCU over UART (UART init strings, TX-A/TX-B) and what messages it exchanges
entries.next_hardware_step: Board-level inspection of the second MCU (DEFERRED_REQUIRES_HARDWARE)

entries.question: Why do the V41 / V3600 packages carry two .ufw sub-images?
evidence: slot A and slot B app.bin SHA-256 identical within each package; isd_config.ini differs (chip key 6413 vs 13462); uboot/cfg_tool/p11 identical
entries.answer: The pair is the same application packaged for two chip-key production variants; the raw images differ in ~80% of bytes purely because of ENC keying.

entries.question: Is the F7 step-length value ever produced by the firmware?
evidence: app.bin string corpus contains 'xbox info:step=%d', 'jstep[%d] time=%x,%x' (V41) / 'stepj[%d] time=%d' (V2224)
the app-side provenance work already proved the app consumes an inbound F7 event frame (does not imply the body firmware emits one)
entries.answer: The F7 handler 0x1e08860 reads its payload byte as b[r9+3] (r9 = frame start, so this is payload[0], not a checksum, whenever the frame is longer than 4 bytes). It compares that byte against 2, stores it into state+0x150, and only for the values 0 and 1 continues to 0x1e0642c (the shared builder) on a path that emits opcode 0xF6. A live A5 04 F7 A0 has NO payload byte, so b[r9+3] is the checksum 0xA0, which is neither 0 nor 1 - the handler stores it and exits without emitting anything. This is a STRONG EVIDENCE explanation of the live F7 read silence and is NOT promoted to F7_WRITE_ONLY.
entries.next_offline_step: Locate the F7 opcode arm of the frame dispatcher once FW-U-021 is resolved
entries.next_hardware_step: A guarded, read-only F7 listen experiment (already prepared; NOT tonight)

entries.question: Which instruction set does the AC6321A app use, and how do we disassemble it?
evidence: app base 0x01E00000, entry 0x01E00120, board bd19/ac6321a
SDK cpu/bd19/tools/rom.lst is a full disassembly of the BD19 ROM, annotated 'file format ELF32-q32s' (9,747 parsed instructions; lengths 2/4/6 bytes = 16/32/48-bit)
opcode-prefix enrichment: the 48 most frequent ROM two-byte prefixes occur ~99,000-100,300 times per MiB in every app.bin vs 749 per MiB in random data (approx. 133x)
results/firmware/isa-identification.md
entries.answer: Resolved: the vendor's own q32s disassembler was obtained (JieLi Linux toolchain, LLVM 4.0.1 fork, registered targets pi32/pi32v2/q32s). Wrapping the raw image as an ELF32-q32s section and linking at 0x01e00000 gives a real disassembly. Independent validation: the BD19 ROM reconstructed from rom.lst re-disassembles with 9,746/9,746 exact matches (100.0% text, length and branch-target agreement).

entries.question: How much of the vendor firmware is stock JieLi SDK code?
evidence: ArmorX V41 cfg_tool.bin is byte-identical (SHA-256 0ccc2fd57959...) to the stock AC63 SDK cpu/bd19/tools/cfg_tool.bin
uboot.boot (a64171c3cf41...) and p11_code.bin are byte-identical across all five packages, body and dongle
p11_code.bin differs from the SDK copy (vendor-modified resource)
public repo commits recorded in research/firmware/2026-09-28/tool-provenance.json
entries.answer: The bootloader, config tool and resource blob are shared stock JieLi components; only app.bin and isd_config.ini are vendor-distinct. This makes a stock-SDK-vs-ArmorX app diff the most promising offline route to isolating ArmorX-specific code once the ISA decoder exists.
ruled_out: fully custom vendor toolchain for the boot/config layer
entries.next_offline_step: Diff a stock AC63 SDK demo build's app image against ArmorX app.bin once q32s decoding works

entries.question: Where are the D6, D8, FC, F6, AB and 0B families handled, if not in armorx_cmd_dispatch?
evidence: 0x1e08772 compares only 0x2F/0x70/0xD2/0xD4/0xD7/0xF7/0xF8/0xF9/0xFA/0xFF
0x1e0aff2 compares 0xA5 and 0x0B (three 0B references) and calls the frame handler
0x1e0a944 compares 0x0B twice
results/firmware/armorx-command-dispatch.json
entries.answer: FOUND: 0x0B -> 0x1e089e8, 0x19 -> 0x1e08d24 (state byte, shared with D2), 0x05 -> factory/diagnostic sub-dispatch at 0x1e08e62/0x1e08e78, D6 -> 0x1e0921c, D7 -> 0x1e09232, D8 -> 0x1e0928c, D9 -> 0x1e09346 - all via range-gated tbh tables (0x1e089c4 for 0x0B..0x1B, 0x1e09060 for 0xD4..0xD9, 0x1e08a04 for 0xE1..0xE5) that the previous pass's compare-only extractor could not see. NOT FOUND: FC and F6 do not appear in any of the three tables, and the 0xE6..0xFF branch at 0x1e08e8c accepts only 0xEF, so 0xFC/0xF6 fall to the default handler 0x1e08ff2. AB likewise does not appear in any extracted table. D6/D8/0B are therefore SETTLED and the open part is specifically FC/F6/AB.
entries.next_offline_step: Extract the compare structure of 0x1e0aff2 and 0x1e0a944 (0B lives there), and de-nest the sub-switches in 0x1e08772 to see whether D6/D8/FC are reached under a sub-command byte.

entries.question: Does the handler base register (r9) point at the frame start or at the payload?
evidence: armorx_cmd_dispatch reads payload bytes as b[r9 + 0x2], b[r9 + 0x3], b[r9 + 0x4]
the F7 handler compares b[r9+0x3] against 0x2 and the D4 path reads b[r9+0x3]/b[r9+0x4]
live frames are A5 04 F7 A0 (last byte is the checksum) and A5 04 D4 7D
entries.answer: r9 = FRAME START. The parser prologue fixes it: 0x1e08778 r13 = r0 (context arg), 0x1e0877e r9 = r1 (second argument), and the very first payload access is 0x1e08792 r1 = b[r9 + 0x2], compared immediately against 0x2F/0x70/0xD2/0xD4/0xD7/0xF7/0xF8/0xF9/0xFA/0xFF. In every live frame the opcode sits at frame[2] (A5 04 0B B4, A5 05 D2 01 7D, A5 05 FC 80 26), so r9+0 = magic (0xA5), r9+1 = length, r9+2 = opcode, r9+3.. = payload, and the highest field read anywhere in the parser is r9+7, consistent with the app's longest frame (A5 08 ...). The checksum byte is frame[len-1], which coincides with r9+3 only for 4-byte frames - which is exactly why a bare F7 read looks like a payload write
ruled_out: r9 = parser cursor past the header
entries.next_offline_step: Read the frame handler prologue and its caller to fix r9's origin, then re-read the F7 handler with that base.

entries.question: Which function computes the protocol checksum (live-proven: sum of preceding bytes)?
evidence: frame_err_checksum (0x1e070da) is the checksum-error printer called from the frame handler
0x1e05c66 builds 0xDC-byte records and hashes 8 bytes with '...len=%d crc=%x' (record integrity, not necessarily the frame checksum)
entries.answer: The RECORD integrity routine is now identified: 0x1e05628 is a reflected (LSB-first) nibble-table CRC-16 with init 0xFFFF, and 0x1e0566a is the record-header validator that reads a big-endian length at [2..3], rejects len<4 or len>max, then calls 0x1e05628(ptr+2, len-2) and compares the result against the big-endian value stored at [0..1]. That matches the live-validated CRC-16/MODBUS (poly 0xA001, init 0xFFFF) of the 144-byte config, which is STRONG EVIDENCE that 0x1e05628 is the config CRC. The FRAME level checksum (live-proven to be a plain sum of the preceding bytes) is a different mechanism and its routine is still not identified - it is likely inline, which is why only the error printer (0x1e070da) was found.
entries.next_offline_step: Follow the call made between the length check and the checksum-error branch in 0x1e08772; the callee is the checksum routine.

entries.question: What does the firmware use to decide when a D2 report is sent (the event-driven behaviour)?
evidence: D2 handler entry recovered at 0x1e08d24 (fall-through of the rOP != 0xD2 test)
live: no D2 frames are produced for analog-only change; a digital trigger produces a report carrying both the RT digital bit and the RT analog byte
entries.answer: The D2 handler 0x1e08d24 is now read: it decodes the payload byte (r4 = b[r9+3]) into an enabled value, stores it at state+0x10 (0x19 stores to state+0x11 through the same block), and when the enable condition holds calls 0x1e04b38 (app_select_24g). The D2 REPORT SEND GATE itself (the condition that emits A5 12 02 frames) has still not been read out - it is in the report builder, not in this handler.
entries.next_offline_step: Read 0x1e08d24 and find the dirty-flag/compare that gates report construction, then match it against the capture evidence.

entries.question: Is there a lighting/RGB handler and an identifiable IMU part in the image?
evidence: 'switch_lights=%x' and 'led_check failed, reset setting' strings exist and resolve to code
IMU logic strings exist ('IMU_TYPE_LEFT/RIGHT', 'imu_not calibrated', 'gyro CAL data now:%d,%d,%d')
no WHO_AM_I value, I2C address or IMU part number appears in the plaintext strings
entries.answer: Not answered. The strings prove the subsystems exist; no opcode family or part identity is established.
entries.next_offline_step: Trace the callers of 0x1e1569a (gyro calibration) for the sensor bus accesses, and find the opcode family that reaches the switch_lights code.

entries.question: Why does the CRC routine load its table from 0x1e29900 when the CRC-16/MODBUS nibble table is at 0x1e297e0?
evidence: 0x1e05632: r2 = 0x1e29900 (immediate bytes c2 ff 00 99 e2 01)

the reflected CRC-16/MODBUS nibble table (16 halfwords: 0000 cc01 d801 1400 f001 3c00 2800 e401 a001 6c00 7800 b401 5000 9c01 8801 4400) occurs exactly once in the image, at file offset 0x297e0 = address 0x1e297e0, delta 0x120
the bytes at 0x1e29900 are the assert string 'P33 SYS SOFT RESET : P3_PR_PWR[4]=1' followed by 'soft_reset_exception'/'soft_reset_assert'
string xrefs elsewhere are not shifted (0x1e2754c is 'n=%d crc=%x' exactly as the corpus says), so this is not a global file/address offset
entries.answer: Not answered. Either the routine's table is populated at runtime at 0x1e29900 (over the assert pool) or the immediate is a stale/unrelocated address. Practical implication: record CRC values must be computed with the live-validated algorithm, not by reading the table at whatever address an immediate names.
ruled_out: a global file-offset/relocation shift for the whole image
entries.next_offline_step: Trace any startup copy whose destination is 0x1e29900 with source 0x1e297e0

entries.question: Why does the firmware 0xD6 handler return a single 16-bit value when the live capture showed a 144-byte D6 read?
evidence: 0x1e0921c (the only 0xD6 target in every extracted dispatch table) reads [state+0x1b0], extracts the big-endian 16-bit field at +2..3 and replies with opcode 0xD6 - it never inspects the payload or loop over fragments
live: the D6 read returned 144 bytes in 9x20 + 1x14 byte fragments and D7 was verified against that 144-byte SHA
entries.answer: Not answered. Either the live 144-byte read was attributed to the wrong opcode, or a second 0xD6 path exists outside the parser (for example a config-engine entry reached from the 0x2F..0xE0 chain rather than from the D4..D9 table). Do NOT treat the live 'D6 = 144-byte read' label as firmware-confirmed until this is closed.
entries.next_offline_step: Read the 0x2F..0xE0 chain arms that do not dispatch to the D4..D9 table, and the 0x1e0aff2/0x1e0a944 hotspots, looking for a second 0xD6 compare

entries.question: Why does the 0x0B handler load the constant 0x32 (50) when the live reply payload was 0x30 (48)?
evidence: 0x1e089e8: r0 = 0x32; b[sp+4] = r0; r2 = sp+4; r1 = 0xb; goto 0x1e08e5a (TX tail) - r1 = 0x0B confirms the case-to-opcode mapping
live: A5 04 0B B4 -> A5 05 0B 30 E5, i.e. payload 0x30 and checksum 0xE5 = 0xA5+0x05+0x0B+0x30
entries.answer: Not answered. The 2-count difference may be a later adjustment on the TX path or a different runtime value; the live value is the authoritative one.
entries.next_offline_step: Follow the 0x1e08e5a TX tail with r1 = 0x0B and r2 = buffer
